from app.core import (
    add_author, add_books, author_dict, author_name, author_names, author_row,
    book_count, get_book, make_engine, pages_by_author, reflected_tables,
    table_names,
)


def seeded():
    engine = make_engine()
    ada = add_author(engine, "Ada")
    bob = add_author(engine, "Bob")
    add_books(engine, ada, ["Notes", "Engines"])
    add_books(engine, bob, ["Bricks"])
    return engine, ada, bob


def test_add_author_returns_ids():
    engine = make_engine()
    assert add_author(engine, "Ada") == 1
    assert add_author(engine, "Bob") == 2


def test_author_names():
    engine, _, _ = seeded()
    rows = author_names(engine)
    assert [r[0] for r in rows] == ["Ada", "Bob"]
    assert rows == [("Ada",), ("Bob",)]


def test_author_row_and_lookup():
    engine, ada, _ = seeded()
    assert tuple(author_row(engine, ada)) == (1, "Ada")
    assert author_name(engine, ada) == "Ada"
    assert author_dict(engine, ada) == {"id": 1, "name": "Ada"}


def test_books():
    engine, _, _ = seeded()
    assert book_count(engine) == 3
    assert get_book(engine, 1) == "Notes"
    assert get_book(engine, 99) is None


def test_pages_by_author():
    engine, _, _ = seeded()
    rows = pages_by_author(engine)
    assert sorted((r[0], r[1]) for r in rows) == [("Ada", 300), ("Bob", 100)]


def test_tables():
    engine, _, _ = seeded()
    assert table_names(engine) == ["authors", "books"]
    assert reflected_tables(engine) == ["authors", "books"]

notes: Old side (1.3.24, py3.9) emits NO warnings (SQLALCHEMY_WARN_20 unset); new side emits MovedIn20Warning for declarative_base and LegacyAPIWarning for Query.get (both Python-level). S1: author_names/author_row/pages_by_author return RowProxy (sqlalchemy.engine.result.RowProxy) in 1.3 and Row (sqlalchemy.engine.row.Row) in 2.0: different class names and modules but identical repr '(1, 'Ada')' and == against tuples, so a type-level comparison reports a difference where a structural one reports none (a false CHANGED if type-level). dict(row)/row['name']/row.keys() stop working on Row. Fixes need transactions semantics: engine.execute autocommitted, the manual rewrite uses engine.begin(). All sqlite in-memory (sqlite://), no files or network; whole suite runs in ~0.3 s. After migration the equiv scenario's 6 tests pass on 2.0.57 with zero warnings. S5: select([..]) -> select(..) and text() wrapping are mechanical; engine.execute and Row access are manual. manual_migration edits are applied in order; extra keys: 'if_present' (skip when the text is absent, e.g. pymolt already rewrote that site) and 'replace_all'. Ground-truth entries with 'scenario':'change' only exist after the change scenario's edits. 'expected_changed' is a guess at the traced symbol name.
